patterns: Each language is a single handler file with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY constants (java.rs, swift.rs); optional queries are Option<&str> in LanguageInfo.

extract_inheritance walks named children of a clause node (java.rs superclass/interfaces; swift.rs inheritance_specifier) and emits prefixed strings such as 'extends X' and 'implements X'.

Java DEFUSE_QUERY pattern: declaration-site captures tagged write.local, assignment captures tagged write.assign, update captures tagged writeread.update, and a catch-all (identifier) @read.usage; parser_elements.rs classifies by capture-name prefix (lines 874-886).

constraints: External PRs are not accepted for #1864; the maintainers implement it in-house (issue 'Note on Process').

Scope limits from the issue: .php only (no .phtml, .inc, .module, .php5); no trait use resolution, property or constant extraction, attributes or namespace alias import; no tool handler or schema changes; no other languages.

php must be in supported_languages() (lang.rs:81-99) because parser.rs QUERY_CACHE (parser.rs:191) is built only from that list and get_compiled_queries (parser.rs:221) returns UnsupportedLanguage for anything missing from it.

Gap found in existing code (read-only, not run): css and yaml are wired in get_language_info() and get_ts_language() and EXTENSION_MAP, but are absent from supported_languages(), so the same QUERY_CACHE path would reject them. PHP must not copy that omission; fixing css and yaml is outside #1864 scope.

DEFUSE_QUERY: the issue's scope and acceptance list require it, and the registry treats defuse_query as Option (parser.rs:159 compiles it only when Some; parser_elements.rs:850 returns no sites when None). Nothing in production calls it: parser.rs:547 and parser_elements.rs:840 both say 'No production caller since the symbol tool removal; retained for language tests.' So it is required by the contract, not by runtime behaviour.

Cargo.lock age rule (issue): new entries must be at least 7 days old (AGENTS.md). GitHub release v0.25.2 of tree-sitter-php was published 2026-11-19T16:26:36Z, 8 days before this run; v0.25.1 was published 2026-10-06T16:47:06Z. crates.io publish dates were not verifiable from this environment, so check the crates.io timestamp before locking 0.25.2; 0.25.1 is the safe fallback.

Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY: the php-dialect program rule (define-grammar.js lines 166-175) accepts optional text and php_tag, which the mixed-HTML acceptance criterion needs; I did not inspect the php_only branch in detail.

tree-sitter-php 0.25.x depends only on tree-sitter-language (0.1.x) at runtime, and its dev-dependency is tree-sitter 0.27; the lock already has tree-sitter 0.27.2 and tree-sitter-language 0.1.9, so no duplicate tree-sitter should appear. Its build.rs compiles php/src/parser.c and scanner.c with the cc crate (C toolchain required at build time).
Binary size delta must be stated in the PR description (issue acceptance; #1063). Adding a grammar adds compiled parser C code.
Query and capture naming must match parser_elements.rs consumers (function, class, func_name, method_name, class_name, type_name), or the element counts silently stay at zero.

Lib doc lists also enumerate languages (crates/aptu-coder-core/src/lib.rs:11, languages/mod.rs:7, crates/aptu-coder/src/lib.rs:23, crates/aptu-coder-core/README.md:22 and :66). The issue scopes only README.md; leave the others alone unless the maintainers widen scope.

approaches.name: A: Full registry integration mirroring Java and Swift (recommended)
approaches.description: Add languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name based), and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Wire 'php' into get_language_info() and get_ts_language() with tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP, add ('php','php') to EXTENSION_MAP and to supported_languages(), add tree-sitter-php to both Cargo.toml files and Cargo.lock, add a README entry and the 18-to-19 count, and add unit tests in php.rs plus a table row in mod.rs and an extension row in lang.rs, and an integration test file under crates/aptu-coder/tests/.
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in #1864, including extends/implements and the mixed-HTML case.
Same five-constant shape as java.rs, so reviewers and parser_elements consumers see no new contract.
Grammar node kinds and fields are verified against php/src/node-types.json and define-grammar.js, so the queries can be checked in the unit tests before wiring.
Inheritance walk is by kind, which avoids depending on unfielded children.
cons: Cargo.lock and C build of parser.c/scanner.c increase build time and binary size; the delta must be reported.
DEFUSE_QUERY has no production consumer, so its tests only cover the retained extract_def_use path.
Qualified base names keep the leading backslash in the text, which some consumers may not expect.

approaches.name: B: Minimal query-only handler
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY only; set reference_query, defuse_query and extract_inheritance to None in LanguageInfo; wire the same registry, Cargo and README entries as A.
pros: Smallest code change and the fewest unit tests to write.
Gets functions, classes, calls and imports working quickly for the common case.
cons: Fails the issue's acceptance criteria for extends/implements (extract_inheritance must return the listed strings) and the five-constant contract (DEFUSE_QUERY required).
Leaves class inheritance empty, which the ClassInfo.inherits field would expose as an empty list for every PHP class.
Would need a follow-up PR, which the in-house maintainers would have to schedule.

approaches.name: C: Full integration plus receiver handlers and php_only dialect
approaches.description: Approach A plus extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type copied from java.rs, and LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY instead of LANGUAGE_PHP so the grammar is smaller and only handles pure PHP files.
pros: Parity with the Java handler set (all optional handler slots filled).
php_only grammar avoids text and php_tag handling, so parser size may shrink slightly.
cons: Receiver handlers are explicitly out of scope in #1864 and have no consumer since #1807, so this is dead code.
php_only rejects the mixed-HTML template case the issue requires to parse with zero ERROR nodes.
More code to review and test, with no acceptance benefit.

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets every acceptance criterion in #1864 (inheritance strings, DEFUSE_QUERY present, mixed HTML via LANGUAGE_PHP) while mirroring the Java template and the registry wiring that css and swift use. Before locking, (1) add 'php' to supported_languages() as well as EXTENSION_MAP, because the omission of css and yaml there is the one trap in the existing wiring; (2) confirm the crates.io publish timestamp for tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 is at least 7 days old, or pin 0.25.1; (3) treat DEFUSE_QUERY as a contract-level requirement with no runtime consumer.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source inspected: php/grammar.js delegates to common/define-grammar.js (fetched with gh api, 1738 lines); php/src/node-types.json (305 types, 114258 bytes) confirms child kinds. (1) class_declaration rule, define-grammar.js lines 365-373, verbatim: seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list)). node-types.json lists class_declaration fields as only attributes, body, name; base_clause and class_interface_clause are UNFIELDED children, so child_by_field_name() cannot reach them. The walk must iterate node.child(i) / named children and match on kind(). (2) extends: for each child with kind() == "base_clause" (rule lines 334-337: seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name))), iterate its named children; node-types.json lists base_clause children as name, qualified_name, relative_name (the hidden _name choice, lines 296-302). Emit format!("extends {text}") for each. The keyword token 'extends' is anonymous and is skipped by named_child iteration. (3) implements: for each child with kind() == "class_interface_clause" (rule lines 381-384: seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name))), iterate named children with the same kinds (node-types.json confirms name, qualified_name, relative_name); emit format!("implements {text}") for each. (4) The field 'body' (declaration_list) is skipped by the kind() filter. Per-kind coverage: interface_declaration (lines 326-332) has an optional base_clause and so maps to a list of 'extends' entries; enum_declaration (lines 339-346) has no base_clause, only an optional class_interface_clause (implements) plus an optional ': string|int' primitive_type that the kind filter ignores; trait_declaration (lines 319-324) has no clauses and returns an empty Vec. Expected for 'class Foo extends Bar implements A, B': ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; with no clause: []. Text is the raw source slice, so a fully qualified base such as \Lib\Base keeps its leading backslash (same convention as Java's type_identifier slices).
